items.title: DD News promoted E20 using seven pro-govt farmer leaders without disclosing their ties
items.summary: A nationwide debate is raging over ethanol-blended petrol, or E20, with motorists complaining of lower mileage and alleged engine damage. The government, meanwhile, has stuck to a central defence: E20 is good for farmers. DD News has been an enthusiastic vehicle for that message. Since May, the public broadcaster has aired more than 50 explainers, debates and ground reports promoting E20. But last month, it went a step further, publishing videos of seven farmer leaders on its official social media accounts, all making essentially the same case: ethanol blending is driving farmers’ progress. There was something else these seven had in common. All were already supporters of the Modi government and its policies. Several had backed the three farm laws at the centre of the 2020–21 farmers’ protest, and some had openly opposed the agitation. So, in other words, as criticism of E20 mounted, DD News turned to seven farmer leaders with established pro-government positions to bolster its case for ethanol blending, without disclosing those affiliations to its audience. items.title: Karnataka SIR draft rolls are out: What voters need to do next
items.summary: The draft electoral rolls for Karnataka were published on Monday, August 24, marking the next phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the state's voter list. Voters have until September 23 to file claims and objections but even after that window shuts, the process isn't final: people whose claims are rejected can apply again under Form 6, according to Karnataka’s Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukumar. The draft roll contains 4.46 crore electors, compared with 5.54 crore electors on the roll as of June 16. More than 1.07 crore electors from the earlier roll have not been included in the draft and have instead been placed under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate or Others (ASDDO) category during the enumeration exercise. However, being left out of the draft roll does not mean that a voter's name has been permanently deleted. The Election Commission has opened a claims and objections period from August 24 to September 23, during which eligible electors can seek inclusion, correct their details or object to wrongful inclusions. items.title: Delay in disqualifying rebel TMC MPs: SC seeks reply to plea by Abhishek Banerjee against Speaker's inaction

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the rebel MPs and sought their responses but refrained from issuing notice to Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla, the main respondent in the matter. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana Around 20 MPs who had won on TMC ticket had defected to the relatively unknown NCPI in June this year after rebelling against the leadership of party supremo Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee. This was immediately after TMC lost the assembly elections in West Bengal which led to discontent within the party. When the plea by Banerjee came up for hearing on Tuesday, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Central government, requested the Court not to issue notice to the Lok Sabha speaker. "I have some reservations about issuing notice to the Speaker," he said.

items.title: You can't train law students to argue by curbing their free speech: Prof Faizan Mustafa
items.summary: Chanakya National Law University (CNLU) Vice-Chancellor (VC) Prof Faizan Mustafa said on Monday that law students can't be trained in the art of argument when their freedom of speech is curbed. He added that law students and law schools, in his assessment, allow their students considerably greater freedom of expression than Vice-Chancellors of traditional universities typically permit. "I am absolutely clear that since law students are going to defend liberties of others, they are to be trained in this art of making an argument and you cannot train them in the art of argument by curbing their freedom of speech in terms of speaking, in terms of making cartoons, or in terms of every other expression," he said. Prof Mustafa was speaking at a webinar titled Freedom of speech in law schools , hosted by The Hindu. He was responding to a question on recent convocation row at the National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law and its subsequent fallout. He was also asked how he would have reacted had his own students opposed the Chief Justice of India (CJI) as chief guest at their convocation. items.title: Rs 428 crore in, Rs 1 crore out: How Chinese capital and public money vanished into Gurugram’s garbage
items.summary: In 2017, Ecogreen was hired to collect and process garbage in Gurugram and Faridabad, and to reduce the enormous Bandhwari landfill. A Chinese company invested Rs 428 crore in Ecogreen, and the government paid it another Rs 157 crore. But the promised waste-to-energy plant was never built and the landfill grew into a 38-metre-high garbage mountain, polluting the groundwater of nearby villages. Company records show that large sums went to related companies, consultancy fees and advances for machinery that never arrived. In 2024, the government cancelled Ecogreen’s contract and its Chinese owner sold the company for just Rs 1 crore. Ecogreen is only part of a larger problem: waste management in Gurugram has become an endless garbage contract, with one company after another failing to deliver as public spending and garbage pile up. *** Start at the end. In the summer of 2024, a Chinese firm that runs waste-to-energy plants sold its entire Indian business for Rs 1 crore – about the price of a modest flat in the city it had been hired to clean. A Division Bench of Justice Saumitra Dayal Singh and Justice Swarupama Chaturvedi declared Sections 8, 9, 10, 38 and 42 of the Act ultra vires. The Court held that Sections 8, 9 and 10 – which pertain to payment of rent and its revision - were repugnant to the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. “As to the rent payable, Section 8 allows that revision of the same in terms of Section 9 and for its determination in terms of Section 10. First, revision may arise in terms of the tenancy agreement as may also the case under TPA, but then provisions exist under the Impugned Act to provide for upward revision of the rent at specified rates. Also, Section 10 provides for determination of revised rent in the case of the dispute between the landlord and the tenant i.e. lessor and lessee that is completely in conflict with the provisions of TPA,” the Bench observed.
